title: Tenali Raman and the Three Axes
summary: On the outskirts of Vijayanagara, a poor, honest woodcutter named Kariappa was chopping firewood along the steep, rocky banks of the Tungabhadra River. His old iron axe slipped ...
full_text:
On the outskirts of Vijayanagara, a poor, honest woodcutter named Kariappa was chopping firewood along the steep, rocky banks of the Tungabhadra River. His old iron axe slipped from his sweaty hands and plummeted into the deep, swirling water.
Having no money to buy another tool to feed his hungry family, Kariappa sat upon the riverbank and wept with bitter sorrow.

Tenali Raman, who was walking along the river path, heard his weeping.
Learning of his plight, Tenali dove into the deep pool.
A moment later, Tenali surfaced holding an axe forged of glittering, solid gold!
'Is this thy axe, good man?' asked Tenali.

Kariappa looked at the dazzling gold, shook his head honestly, and said:
'No, noble sir. That axe is made of gold; it belongs to a king. My axe was an ordinary tool of rusted iron with a worn neem-wood handle.'

Tenali dove a second time, surfacing with an axe crafted of pure, polished silver with an ebony handle:
'Is this thy axe?'
Kariappa replied:
'No, master. That is of silver; I cannot claim what is not mine.'

Tenali dove a third time, bringing up Kariappa’s old, rusted iron axe.
Kariappa leaped with joy, tears of relief in his eyes:
'Yes! That is my axe! That is the breadwinner of my family!'

Tenali, moved by the woodcutter's rare, incorruptible honesty, presented him with all three axes—the gold, the silver, and the iron—along with a bag of grain, saying:
'Honesty like thine is worth more than all the gold in the river.'

Kariappa returned to his village, prosperous and happy.
Hearing of his fortune, an envious, greedy neighbor named Somanna took his own iron axe, ran to the same riverbank, threw his axe into the water, and sat down to weep fake tears.

Tenali Raman, watching from behind a tree, dove into the water and brought out a magnificent golden axe:
'Is this thy axe, friend?'
Somanna snatched greedily at the golden tool, shouting:
'Yes, yes! That is my axe! Give it to me!'

Tenali pulled the golden axe back, his eyes flashing with righteous disdain:
'Thou art a liar and a cheat! This gold belongs to the river, and since thou hast lied, thou shalt not even have thine own iron axe back!'

Tenali threw the golden axe back into the deep current, leaving the greedy cheat with empty hands, weeping real tears of regret over his lost tool, proving that greed reaps only loss, while honesty inherits the earth.
moral: Uncompromising honesty receives lasting honor, while greedy imitation reaps only empty hands.
